findings.title: Possible TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null. The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. For a Google Meet location with no destination calendar, `create()` throws instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Selected calendar lookup depends on credentialId, with a fallback that can write to the wrong calendar
findings.body: createEvent now picks the target calendar by matching `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. EventManager calls `createEvent(c, event)` with no externalId when the destination has no credentialId. A destination that lacks credentialId never matches, so the event goes to "primary", which can be wrong. Also, the patch call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is undefined when there is no match, instead of the "primary" fallback used for insert. The hangout-link patch then fails.

findings.title: Dead and tautological destination lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent
findings.body: The code is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In the else branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find compares against a falsy value and returns nothing useful. The original fallback to the destination calendar's externalId was lost, so updates and deletes without an explicit id no longer reach the destination calendar. This also affects `deleteEvent` at line 317.

findings.title: Mutating a shared array, and an array that may be null, when adding team destination calendars
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when the organizer has no calendar, because destinationCalendar is then `null`. In that case the team members' calendars are silently dropped. teamDestinationCalendars is filled inside async map callbacks, which run synchronously up to the first await, so the ordering works only by accident. Also, a collective host whose destination calendar duplicates the organizer's will get duplicate events.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite changes behavior
findings.body: The rewrite drops `organization: { select: { slug } }` from the dynamic user query. It also now throws for an empty dynamicUserList and wraps every error as an HttpError 400 or 500. These changes are unrelated to the fix and can break dynamic group bookings and anything that reads `user.organization`.

findings.title: Inverted slug logic with no explanation
findings.body: The change from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` flips behavior. The org slug is now set only when team billing is enabled, and requestedSlug is unchanged. This is unrelated to the PR and looks like a regression for self-hosted instances without billing, because the org is created with no slug.

findings.title: Unrelated user-visible string change
findings.body: The string "Notes have been hidden by the organiser" was changed to "organizer" in an unrelated edit. Any tests or consumers that match the old text will break.
